_comment: The first WER ledger entry egs/mini_librispeech/asr has ever had.
Everything here comes from one run, 46100161743, and that is the most
important thing to know about it. yesno's entry has a reference_wer
from the author's own pre-refactor CUDA runs to judge against; this
recipe has never published a WER, so there is nothing historical to
compare with and measured_wer is the only anchor that exists.
**The gate is therefore wider than the evidence justifies, and that is
deliberate.** One run gives no estimate of run-to-run spread. The
decode is deterministic given a checkpoint -- every nj from 1 to 8
gives byte-identical hypotheses -- but the training that produces the
checkpoint is not bit-reproducible across runners, and this model is
undertrained and on a steep part of its curve, where a small
difference in the optimisation lands somewhere visibly different. So
max_wer is measured_wer plus two points, and the second recorded run
is what should tighten it. Two points is 403 word errors of 20,138,
which is 4.3% relative: far too loose to catch a subtle regression and
tight enough to catch the kind this corpus exists to catch -- a
broken feature pipeline, a topology that stopped composing, a decoder
that deletes everything.
Judge a change against measured_wer, not against max_wer. **Raising
max_wer to make a run pass is how a ledger stops meaning anything.**
Only `ctc` is recorded. The other seven topologies have never been
trained on this corpus: at 36 minutes an epoch, eight epochs of one
topology is five and a half hours, so all eight would be days. A
topology absent from `topologies` is unmeasured, not passing.
**Two decoders scored the same checkpoint, and the Python one is the
measurement.** `measured_wer` is BenNevis's own search in
BenNevis/decode/viterbi.py, because that is the system's output now.
Kaldi's decode-faster read the same log probabilities against its own
TLG.fst and is recorded beside it as `kaldi_wer` -- a cross-check on
the whole graph and search chain rather than a gate, and one that
will disappear with Kaldi.
reference_source: none: this recipe has no published pre-refactor WER

training.note: Still falling at epoch 8, by 0.028 -- flattening rather than bottomed. The last three improvements were 0.080, 0.036 and 0.028, so a ninth epoch would buy something and the run had no budget for it: 5h34m of a 5h50m ceiling. A deeper model is the thing to change, not the epoch count.

measured.note: CPU, torch 2.15, SpecAugment off, 8 epochs of ctc, 36.6 minutes an epoch. Kaldi's stage 7 decoded all 1,089 utterances in 7m07s at nj=8; the Python search took 20m38s at nj=8 after a 55s graph build, so 2.9x at 2.24 points better.

features.note: The first ledger entry in this project measured on the features the recipe actually has. yesno's predates dropping pitch and says so; this one does not need the caveat.
